q-40562.html:
Question 1
?

Rounded to two decimal places, what is the acute angle between the vectors v=[18−2−3] and w=[4121]?

a
84.32∘
b
 83.24∘
c
 85.35∘
d
 87.24∘
e
 87.27∘
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Using the formula

cos⁡θ=v⋅w‖v‖‖w‖,

we have the following:

cos⁡θ=v1w1+v2w2+v3w3+v4w4v12+v22+v32+v42w12+w22+w32+w42=(1)(4)+(8)(1)+(−2)(2)+(−3)(1)12+(8)2+(−2)2+(−3)2(4)2+12+(2)2+12=12220=12110=110220

Therefore, θ=arccos⁡(110220)≈87.27∘.

q-40886.name: Question 2
q-40886.problem: Let $A(1,-1,2,0)$, $B(1,0,0,-1)$, and $C(0,1,1,0).$ Find the cosine of the angle $∠BAC.$
q-40886.worked_solution:
Let $v=\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $w=\overset{\to }{AC}.$ Then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =b-a \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}w & =c-a \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Let $\theta =m∠BAC$ be the angle between the vectors $v$ and $w.$ Then, we can find $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ using the following formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{v\cdot w}{‖v‖\,‖w‖} \\  & =\frac{{v}_{1}{w}_{1}+{v}_{2}{w}_{2}+{v}_{3}{w}_{3}+{v}_{4}{w}_{4}}{\sqrt{{v}_{1}^{2}+{v}_{2}^{2}+{v}_{3}^{2}+{v}_{4}^{2}}\,\sqrt{{w}_{1}^{2}+{w}_{2}^{2}+{w}_{3}^{2}+{w}_{4}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{0\cdot (-1)+1\cdot 2+(-2)\cdot (-1)+(-1)\cdot 0}{\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+(-1)^{2}}\,\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{4}{\sqrt{6}\cdot \sqrt{6}} \\  & =\frac{4}{6} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

q-40902.name: Question 3
q-40902.problem: Let $A(-2,1,0,-3)$ and $B(1,-1,1,-4).$ Find the cosine of the angle $∠AOB$, where $O(0,0,0,0)$ is the origin.
q-40902.worked_solution:
First, let

$$
\begin{aligned}a=\overset{\to }{OA}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\,b=\overset{\to }{OB}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1 \\ -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Also, let $\theta =m∠AOB$ be the angle between the vectors $a$ and $b.$ Then, we can find $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ using the following formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{a\cdot b}{‖a‖\,‖b‖} \\  & =\frac{{a}_{1}{b}_{1}+{a}_{2}{b}_{2}+{a}_{3}{b}_{3}+{a}_{4}{b}_{4}}{\sqrt{{a}_{1}^{2}+{a}_{2}^{2}+{a}_{3}^{2}+{a}_{4}^{2}}\,\sqrt{{b}_{1}^{2}+{b}_{2}^{2}+{b}_{3}^{2}+{b}_{4}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{(-2)\cdot 1+1\cdot (-1)+0\cdot 1+(-3)\cdot (-4)}{\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}+(-3)^{2}}\,\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-4)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{9}{\sqrt{14}\cdot \sqrt{19}} \\  & =\frac{9}{\sqrt{266}}\end{aligned}
$$

q-74111.name: Question 4
q-74111.problem: Let $A(1,0,1,0)$ and $B(-1,4,0,-1).$ Find the cosine of the angle $∠AOB$, where $O(0,0,0,0)$ is the origin.
q-74111.worked_solution:
First, let

$$
\begin{aligned}a=\overset{\to }{OA}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,b=\overset{\to }{OB}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 4 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Also, let $\theta =m∠AOB$ be the angle between the vectors $a$ and $b.$ Then, we can find $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ using the following formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{a\cdot b}{‖a‖\,‖b‖} \\  & =\frac{{a}_{1}{b}_{1}+{a}_{2}{b}_{2}+{a}_{3}{b}_{3}+{a}_{4}{b}_{4}}{\sqrt{{a}_{1}^{2}+{a}_{2}^{2}+{a}_{3}^{2}+{a}_{4}^{2}}\,\sqrt{{b}_{1}^{2}+{b}_{2}^{2}+{b}_{3}^{2}+{b}_{4}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{1\cdot (-1)+0\cdot 4+1\cdot 0+0\cdot (-1)}{\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}}\,\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{4}^{2}+{0}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{-1}{\sqrt{2}\cdot \sqrt{18}} \\  & =\frac{-1}{\sqrt{36}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{6}\end{aligned}
$$
